title: Credential Governor: per-scope issuance UI and retention automation
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Goal: Ship a 'Credential Governor' feature that centralizes issuance and lifecycle controls for API keys and service tokens. The Governor provides a UI and API for creating per-scope credentials with enforced naming templates, default lifetimes (ephemeral vs. long-lived), retention policies, and automated deprecation/rotation workflows. It must emit rich audit events for each issuance and lifecycle action, integrate with RBAC v2 role groups and SSO/SAML identity attributes, and provide an admin-facing retention automation engine that retires keys according to policy with a safe rollback path.

Why now: We have a proliferation of long-lived and unscoped keys in customer accounts and internal services. This increases blast radius on credential leakage and makes audit/rotation enforcement manual and error-prone. The Governor reduces operator toil, makes naming and scoping consistent, and ties issuance to Teams/Projects for better telemetry and cost attribution.

Non-goals: full credential broker replacement for external identity providers, realtime secret streaming to workloads (out of scope), building new KMS/HSM features (we'll use existing KMS integrations).
acceptance_criteria: Admin console has a Credential Governor page where admins can choose issuance templates (ephemeral, project-scoped long-lived, service-bound) and create keys via UI or API
Issuance enforces naming templates and scope tags; attempts to create keys that don't match templates are rejected with a clear error code
Default TTLs and rotation reminders apply according to policy and are visible in the UI; retention automation auto-expunges keys past grace period
All lifecycle events (create, view metadata, rotate, revoke, expire) are emitted to audit logging with consistent schema and include actor, template, scope, and correlation_id
Governor integrates with RBAC v2: only principals in allowed role groups (derived from SSO/SAML assertions) can create keys under certain templates
Migration shim supports bulk reconciling of existing unscoped keys into scoped templates with an opt-in mapping workflow and non-disruptive rotation flow
End-to-end tests exist for UI flows, API flows, audit event generation, and retention automation with simulated time advance
Design doc, runbook, and security review completed and attached to the ticket
notes_and_decisions: Decision: Use existing KMS envelope encryption and audit pipeline (OpenTelemetry->log-ingest) — do not add a new KMS integration in this scope.
Decision: Two issuance modes: ephemeral (default short TTL, auto-delete) and long-lived (requires explicit justification and an approver group).
Decision: Naming template format: <team>-<env>-<purpose>-<random6>. Governor will validate against regex and offer a UI generator.
Trade-off: Enforcing strict name-only migration will break some legacy automation. We will provide a 'migration mapping' tool rather than brute rejection on create for the first rollout phase.

Security review notes: emergency global revoke must be callable by SRE/security with additional audit context; implementation will reuse existing emergency revoke endpoint and add Governor scoping flags.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Console-only feature for internal Redwood orgs. UI + audit events + API gate, retention automation disabled. Duration: 2 weeks.
Phase 2 (pilot): Enable retention automation for non-production orgs; add RBAC v2 group enforcement. Duration: 3 weeks.
Phase 3 (general availability): Enable in production, publish docs, enable migration wizard for existing keys, and flip default policy to 'enforce templates' for new organizations after 2 weeks.

Fallback: Feature flag to disable Governor enforcement and revert to legacy issuance. Rollback involves toggling flag and running a reconciliation job to un-tether any jobs depending on governor metadata.
migration_steps: Inventory: Run token inventory job to classify keys as scoped, unscoped, expired, or orphaned (ownerless).
Mapping UI: Provide a mapping assistant in console to attach unscoped keys to a template and owner. This will not rotate keys immediately; it only tags them for policy enforcement.

Rotation window: For mapped legacy keys, trigger a scheduled rotation where the system creates a new scoped key and swaps consumers via a staged rollout or manual swapping instructions depending on environment.
Opt-out: Customers can opt-out of automated rotation per-key for a defined period via the Governor UI; audit events must capture opt-out reason and approver.
Decommission: After grace period and successful verification, delete legacy keys and mark as retired in audit logs.
comments: 2025-02-13 - Maya Patel: Added scope and naming requirements after security sync. Asked SRE to validate emergency revoke reuse.
2025-02-25 - Liam O'Connor: Prototyped UI mockups uploaded to Confluence. Link posted in attachments. Need PM sign-off on naming regex and default TTLs.

2025-03-02 - Priya Desai (Product): Agreed to conservative defaults: ephemeral TTL = 12 hours, long-lived TTL = 365 days with mandatory approver. Added label 'requires-legal-review' for some industries.

2025-03-05 - Security (review): Requested explicit audit schema contract. We will include 'template_id', 'approver', 'owner_id', 'request_origin' in every event. Action: add audit schema to attachments.
2025-03-09 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented API contract /v1/credentials with draft fields. Opened PR #6123. Canary deploy scheduled 2025-03-14.
risk: Medium. Risks include breaking legacy integrations during strict enforcement and misclassification during migration. Mitigations: phased rollout, mapping assistant, and emergency feature-flag rollback.
qa_plan: Unit tests for naming validator and template enforcement
Integration tests for issuance API and audit event emission (assert schema and mandatory fields)
End-to-end test simulating migration: tag legacy keys, perform rotation, verify consumers swapped in staging
Load test: issue 10k ephemeral keys/hour to verify audit pipeline and retention automation scale
Chaos test: simulate emergency revoke path and confirm Governor metadata included in incident logs
telemetry_events: credential.issue - emitted on create; payload includes actor_id, template_id, scope_tags, ttl_seconds, issuance_mode
credential.rotate - emitted on rotation; includes old_key_id, new_key_id, initiated_by
credential.revoke - emitted on revoke; includes reason, actor_id, correlation_id
credential.expire - emitted on automated expiration by retention automation
